body.statement: Set \(J=2\), \(K=3\), and \(\sigma_{n,1}=\sigma_{n,2}=1\). For \(n\ge16\), the atom table \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\) sums to one and induces \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\) with \(p_{n,1}=p_{n,2}=e_{n,1}=e_{n,2}=1/2\). Its only nonzero selected observed cells, for every \(x\in\{1,2\}\) and \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\), are \[q^1_{n,0,x,k}=1/12,\quad q^1_{n,1,x,k}=1/12+m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/3,\quad q^0_{n,1,x,k}=1/12,\quad q^0_{n,0,x,k}=1/12+m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/3.\] Hence \(\ell_{n,x,k}=h_{n,x,k}=m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/3\), \(m((\Pi_+w_n)_x)=m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/2\), \(b_L((\Pi_+w_n)_x)=0\), and \(b_U((\Pi_+w_n)_x)=m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}/3\). Thus \(M_n=1/8+1/(2\sqrt n)\), \(N_{L,n}=0\), \(N_{U,n}=1/12+1/(3\sqrt n)\), and \(\Theta_{I,n}=[0,2/3]\). The two conditional-contrast covariance blocks are \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,1})\) and \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,2})\); the eigenvalues of \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m)\) are \((2+4m)/3\) with multiplicity four, \((2+4m-4m^2)/3\), and \((1-4m^2)/3\). Consequently every eigenvalue of \(\Sigma_{c,n}\) lies in \([1/4,1]\), and \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\in\mathcal P\) for constants satisfying \(p_0\le1/2\), \(\varepsilon\le1/2\), \(m_0\le1/8\), \(\underline\lambda\le1/4\), and \(\overline\lambda\ge1\).
body.justification: The complete atom calculation shows that changing survivor support and simultaneous cut ties coexist with ordinary instrument overlap and a uniformly nondegenerate raw first stage.
body.gap: This is an internal legality and stress-test result for the main uniform theorem, not a claim that a named published implementation fails.
body.consumer: It gives method developers a reproducible boundary benchmark for testing Job Corps-style implementations without relying on an underdetermined latent law.
body.proof_tex:
\emph{Technique.}  We use direct finite-atom enumeration for the probability and identification calculations, the quotient-rule influence function for conditional multinomial probabilities for the covariance calculation, and an explicit rank-two spectral decomposition for the eigenvalue calculation.

Write \(m_x=m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,x}\).  Because \(n\geq 16\),
\[
0<m_2=n^{-1/2}\leq \frac14,
\qquad
m_1=\frac14.
\]
Consequently all four displayed atom weights in \(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\) are nonnegative.  For each fixed \((x,z,r)\), their sum is
\[
\frac1{48}+\frac1{48}+\frac{m_x}{12}
 +\frac{1/2-m_x}{12}
=\frac1{24}+\frac1{24}=\frac1{12}.
\]
There are three values of \(r\), so \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=z)=1/4\) for each \((x,z)\); summing over the four pairs proves that the table has total mass one.  It also gives
\[
p_{n,x}=\sum_{z=0}^1\frac14=\frac12,
\qquad
e_{n,x}=\frac{P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=1)}{p_{n,x}}
=\frac{1/4}{1/2}=\frac12,
\]
where the division is valid because \(p_{n,x}=1/2>0\).

Conditional on \((X_{n1},Z_{n1})=(x,z)\), the four rows for a fixed \(r\) have probabilities
\[
\frac1{12},\quad \frac1{12},\quad
\frac{m_x}{3},\quad \frac{1/2-m_x}{3},
\]
respectively.  This conditional distribution of
\((D_{n1}(0),D_{n1}(1),S_{n1}(0),S_{n1}(1),Y_{n1}(0),Y_{n1}(1))\)
does not depend on \(z\), which verifies \(\texttt{ass:instrument-exogeneity}\).  The construction in \(\texttt{def:witness-atom-law}\) generates the observed variables as
\(D_{ni}=D_{ni}(Z_{ni})\), \(S_{ni}=S_{ni}(D_{ni})\), and
\(Y_{ni}=Y_{ni}(D_{ni})\) when \(S_{ni}=1\); hence the three consistency assumptions hold.  The potential selection and outcomes in every atom are indexed only by treatment, so \(\texttt{ass:exclusion}\) holds.  The only treatment-type pairs are
\[
(D_{ni}(0),D_{ni}(1))\in\{(1,1),(0,0),(0,1)\},
\]
which proves \(D_{ni}(1)\geq D_{ni}(0)\) and thus \(\texttt{ass:no-defiers}\).  On both complier rows, \(S_{ni}(1)-S_{ni}(0)=0\).  With \(\sigma_{n,x}=1\), this proves the inequality in \(\texttt{ass:weak-selection-monotonicity}\).  Finally, take the observations in each row to be independent copies of this one-unit law, as specified by \(\texttt{ass:iid-row}\).

We next enumerate the observed selected cells.  At \(z=0\), only the always-taker row contributes to \((D,S,Y)=(1,1,k)\), whereas the never-taker and always-selected-complier rows contribute to \((D,S,Y)=(0,1,k)\).  At \(z=1\), the roles are reversed.  Dividing the relevant atom weights by \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=z)=1/4\) yields, for every \(x\in\{1,2\}\) and \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
q^1_{n,0,x,k}=\frac1{12},
\qquad
q^1_{n,1,x,k}=\frac1{12}+\frac{m_x}{3},
\]
\[
q^0_{n,1,x,k}=\frac1{12},
\qquad
q^0_{n,0,x,k}=\frac1{12}+\frac{m_x}{3}.
\]
The four atom types exhaust the support, so these are all the nonzero selected observed cells.  By the definitions of the raw capacities,
\[
\ell_{n,x,k}=q^1_{n,1,x,k}-q^1_{n,0,x,k}=\frac{m_x}{3},
\qquad
h_{n,x,k}=q^0_{n,0,x,k}-q^0_{n,1,x,k}=\frac{m_x}{3}.
\]

Let \(v_x=(\Pi_+w_n)_x\).  Since \(p_{n,x}=1/2\) and the preceding contrasts are nonnegative, projection leaves the block unchanged and
\[
v_x^\ell=v_x^h=\frac{m_x}{6}(1,1,1)^{\prime}.
\]
Thus \(\sum_kv_{x,k}^\ell=\sum_kv_{x,k}^h=m_x/2\), and the definition of \(m(\cdot)\) gives
\[
m(v_x)=\frac{m_x}{2}.
\]
For every \(t\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
\sum_{k\leq t}(v_{x,k}^\ell-v_{x,k}^h)=0,
\qquad
\min\!\left\{\sum_kv_{x,k}^h-\sum_kv_{x,k}^\ell,0\right\}=0.
\]
The explicit lower-capacity formula therefore gives \(b_L(v_x)=0\).  For the upper capacity, there are exactly two coordinates among the conditions \(k<t\) and \(k>t\), for each \(t\in\{0,1,2\}\).  Hence
\[
\sum_{k<t}v_{x,k}^\ell+\sum_{k>t}v_{x,k}^h
=2\frac{m_x}{6}=\frac{m_x}{3},
\]
and, since \(m_x/3\leq m_x/2\), the explicit upper-capacity formula gives \(b_U(v_x)=m_x/3\).

Summing the two cell contributions and substituting \(m_1=1/4\) and \(m_2=n^{-1/2}\) now gives
\[
M_n=\frac{m_1+m_2}{2}=\frac18+\frac1{2\sqrt n},
\qquad
N_{L,n}=0,
\qquad
N_{U,n}=\frac{m_1+m_2}{3}=\frac1{12}+\frac1{3\sqrt n}.
\]
In particular \(M_n>0\), so both endpoint divisions are valid, and
\[
\frac{N_{L,n}}{M_n}=0,
\qquad
\frac{N_{U,n}}{M_n}
=\frac{(m_1+m_2)/3}{(m_1+m_2)/2}=\frac23.
\]
The established exact partial-transport mapping in \(\texttt{def:imported-partialtransport-mapping}\) states that these observed-law functionals are the attained sharp endpoints, rather than defining the causal target to equal them.  It follows that
\[
\Theta_{I,n}=\left[\frac{N_{L,n}}{M_n},\frac{N_{U,n}}{M_n}\right]
=\left[0,\frac23\right].
\]
Under the particular displayed latent coupling, \(Y_{n1}(1)=Y_{n1}(0)\) on every atom.  Moreover,
\[
P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(C_{n1}=1,A_{n1}=1)
=\sum_{x=1}^2p_{n,x}m_x=M_n>0.
\]
Thus its causal target is well defined and equals \(\theta_n=0\), which belongs to the sharp observed-law set above.  Sharpness of the full interval, including attainability of its other points by compatible latent couplings, is supplied by the imported identification result rather than by this one diagonal witness coupling.

It remains to calculate the covariance.  Fix a covariate cell and abbreviate \(m=m_x\),
\[
A=A_m=\frac{1/4+m}{3},
\qquad B=\frac1{12},
\qquad c=A+B.
\]
At \(z=1\), the probabilities of the three selected treated categories are each \(A\), and those of the three selected control categories are each \(B\).  Give the treated indicators sign \(+1\) and the control indicators sign \(-1\).  The resulting signed one-hot vector has mean
\[
v_0=(A,A,A,-B,-B,-B)^{\prime}
\]
and second-moment matrix \(\operatorname{diag}(A,A,A,B,B,B)\).  At \(z=0\), give the treated indicators sign \(-1\) and the control indicators sign \(+1\).  Its mean and second-moment matrix are
\[
v_1=(-B,-B,-B,A,A,A)^{\prime},
\qquad
\operatorname{diag}(B,B,B,A,A,A),
\]
respectively.  The quotient rule for a conditional probability \(P(H\mid C)\) gives influence function
\[
\frac{\mathbf 1\{C\}}{P(C)}\{\mathbf 1\{H\}-P(H\mid C)\}.
\]
Here \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}(X_{n1}=x,Z_{n1}=z)=1/4\).  The two instrument-cell contributions have disjoint supports and conditional mean zero.  Therefore the covariance of the six conditional contrasts under total-sample \(\sqrt n\) scaling is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Sigma_x
&=4\Bigl\{\operatorname{diag}(A,A,A,B,B,B)-v_0v_0^{\prime}\\
&\hspace{28mm}+\operatorname{diag}(B,B,B,A,A,A)-v_1v_1^{\prime}\Bigr\}\\
&=4\{cI_6-v_0v_0^{\prime}-v_1v_1^{\prime}\}
=\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m).
\end{aligned}
\]
For distinct covariate cells, the corresponding influence functions have disjoint supports and mean zero, so their cross-covariance is zero.  Hence \(\Sigma_{c,n}\) is block diagonal with blocks
\(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,1})\) and
\(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m^{\mathrm{wit}}_{n,2})\).

For completeness, we diagonalize each block explicitly.  Let
\[
u_\ell=3^{-1/2}(1,1,1,0,0,0)^{\prime},
\qquad
u_h=3^{-1/2}(0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\prime}.
\]
On the four-dimensional orthogonal complement of
\(\operatorname{span}\{u_\ell,u_h\}\), both \(v_0v_0^{\prime}\) and \(v_1v_1^{\prime}\) vanish, so the eigenvalue is
\[
4c=\frac{2+4m}{3}
\]
with multiplicity four.  In the orthonormal basis \((u_\ell,u_h)\), the matrix
\(v_0v_0^{\prime}+v_1v_1^{\prime}\) is
\[
3\begin{pmatrix}
A^2+B^2&-2AB\\
-2AB&A^2+B^2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its eigenvalues are \(3(A-B)^2\) and \(3(A+B)^2\).  Since
\(A-B=m/3\) and \(A+B=c=(1+2m)/6\), the remaining two eigenvalues of \(\Sigma^{\mathrm{wit}}(m)\) are
\[
4\{c-3(A-B)^2\}=\frac{2+4m-4m^2}{3}
\]
and
\[
4\{c-3(A+B)^2\}=\frac{1-4m^2}{3}.
\]
This proves the asserted spectrum and its multiplicities.

Both witness masses lie in \((0,1/4]\).  On \([0,1/4]\), the first displayed eigenvalue lies in \([2/3,1]\); the second is increasing and lies in \([2/3,11/12]\); and the third is decreasing and lies in \([1/4,1/3]\).  Thus every eigenvalue of \(\Sigma_{c,n}\) lies in \([1/4,1]\), and in particular the entire twelve-dimensional contrast space is nonredundant.

We finally check the numerical restrictions defining \(\mathcal P\).  The equalities \(p_{n,x}=e_{n,x}=1/2\) imply \(p_{n,x}\geq p_0\) when \(p_0\leq1/2\), and
\(\varepsilon\leq e_{n,x}\leq1-\varepsilon\) when \(\varepsilon\leq1/2\).  Also
\[
M_n=\frac18+\frac1{2\sqrt n}\geq\frac18\geq m_0
\]
when \(m_0\leq1/8\).  The spectral calculation verifies
\(\texttt{ass:raw-covariance-band}\) whenever
\(\underline\lambda\leq1/4\) and \(\overline\lambda\geq1\).  Together with the sampling, IV, consistency, exclusion, treatment-monotonicity, and selection-monotonicity checks above, these are every member property in \(\texttt{def:model-class}\).  Therefore \(P_n^{\mathrm{wit}}\in\mathcal P\) under the constants stated in the proposition.
